contexts.text: The most deceitful... are invisible...
Genii... render themselves invisible to their companions; for they who have acted secretly in the world can render themselves invisible in the other life.
They worship a God visible and invisible... AC 9971:2.

They replied that (without idols) their ideas could not be fixed and determined to the invisible God. I told them that the ideas of their thought could be fixed and determined to the invisible God, when they are determined to the Lord, who is the visible God; and that thus a man can be conjoined with the invisible God in thought and affection...
He presented this Trine as one and invisible because Divine... (Thus) his idea of the invisible God was the idea of nature in its firsts...
Under God, see this reference. HH 3:8. HH 82. HH 86. DLW 12. AR 224:7. TCR 159:3. TCR 339. TCR 339:2. TCR 786. TCR 787. SE 4772:2. SE 5742.
For what is invisible does not fall into an idea of thought...
The Lord appears in a Divine angelic form... to those who acknowledge a visible Divine, but not to those who acknowledge an invisible Divine; for the former can see their Divine, but not the latter.
As the Angels do not perceive an invisible Divine, which they call a Divine without form...
Not of those who say that they believe in ail invisible God.
Because the Father is invisible, and thence inaccessible...
(The Dutch) are invisible to all other Spirits...
Like an invisible atmosphere...
Certain ones when on high... were invisible...
Those who are of a celestial genius... are invisible to them...
The evil in the World of Spirits know (how to disappear) by making themselves invisible. A disagreement of love and thought has a like effect.
Thus () present themselves invisible. In the other life he who does not think like another is invisible to him.
Whence he became as it were invisible, not only to me, but also to himself...
To believe in what is invisible is not far from believing in the inmost of nature...
That which proceeds immediately from His Divine Itself does not come to man, because His Divine Itself is invisible, and thence does not fall into the thought... AE 114.
In ancient times... scarcely anyone saw in thought an invisible Divine.
The Lord became invisible, yet He was in a human body...
When anyone has spoken contrary to the affection of any Spirit or Angel... he becomes invisible, and disappears.
